column3: That's a man, isn't it?\nLook at his face.{end_wait}
Please... I can hear you.\nI can't move.{end_wait}
Welcome to Bilibin.{page_break}Please don't stare\nat the tree by the gate.{page_break}Men went into Kolima.\nNone have come back.{end_wait}
Travelers crossed Goma\non their way to Imil.{end_wait}
You saw the tree at the\nentrance, didn't you?{end_now}
Lord McCoy hasn't left\nthe palace in days.{end_wait}
Ever tried heading\nsoutheast from here?{end_now}
The road to Kolima\nis closed by order\nof Lord McCoy.{end_wait}
The man at the gate\nwas one of us.{page_break}Now people won't\neven walk past him.{end_wait}
Was Mt. Aleph really\ndestroyed?{page_break}The sky turned red\nthat night.{end_wait}
There's a lighthouse\nnear Imil.{page_break}No one I know\nhas been inside.{end_wait}
The roads are worse\nsince the eruption.{page_break}Even the woods\naren't safe now.{end_wait}
The timber from Kolima\nnever arrived.{page_break}Neither did the men\nwho were hauling it.{end_wait}
You've seen the barricade\nwe put up on the Kolima\nroad?{end_now}
So you're saying this\nis my fault?{end_now}
Bad time to visit.\nBilibin's on edge.{end_wait}
Imil? In this weather?\nYou'll freeze.{end_wait}
Lady McCoy wanted\na grander palace.{page_break}Now look at what\nit's cost us.{end_wait}
Lord McCoy stays inside.{page_break}People notice when\ntheir lord is afraid.{end_wait}
Who let those children\ninto the palace?{end_wait}
No one will go back\ninto that forest.{end_wait}
He begged for help\nwhile he changed.{page_break}We stood there.\nNone of us moved.{end_wait}
I keep thinking\nabout that red sky.{end_wait}
They say only Adepts\ncan enter the lighthouse.{end_wait}
After the eruption,\nI can't sleep well.{end_wait}
Perhaps we should stop\nbuilding the palace.{end_wait}
If I'd known what\nhappened in Kolima,{page_break}I'd never have\ntaken this job.{end_wait}
If the tree caused this,\nwhy not cut it down?{end_wait}
That tree was a man.{page_break}They say Kolima's\nsacred tree cursed him.{end_wait}
McCoy ordered timber\ncut for the palace.{end_wait}
People blame McCoy.{page_break}They won't say so\nwhile he's listening.{end_wait}
Lady McCoy has\neverything she wants.{page_break}I wonder what\nthat feels like.{end_wait}
Imil's buried in snow.{page_break}Don't go without\nwarm clothes.{end_wait}
We rarely see snow\nin Bilibin.{end_wait}
When spring comes, I'm\ngoing to see that angel\n{actor_name:4} again.{end_wait}
A winter in Imil?\nNo, thank you.{end_wait}
Has anyone heard\nfrom Kolima?{end_wait}
I knew the man\nby the gate.{end_wait}
They say everyone\nin Kolima turned to trees.{end_wait}
I saw him yesterday.{page_break}Today he can't\neven speak.{end_wait}
There's a legend\nabout Hermes' Water.{page_break}They say it can\nheal terrible wounds.{end_wait}
I wonder if it could\nmake me young again.{end_wait}
Could Hermes' Water\nundo the curse?{end_wait}
No one's seen\nHermes' Water in years.{end_wait}
There was a healer\nin Vale, they say.{end_wait}
I wish he were here\nto help us.{end_wait}
Have you ever heard of\nthe ocean?{end_now}
I'd like to see\nthe world someday.{end_wait}
You look capable.{page_break}Perhaps Lord McCoy\nwould speak to you.{end_wait}
It takes courage\nto enter that forest.{end_wait}
Kolima's cursed.\nWhat happens next?{end_wait}
The road is blocked.\nYou can't reach Kolima.{end_wait}
My family lives\nin Kolima.{page_break}I can't work\nwithout thinking of them.{end_wait}
Chef, the customers\nare waiting!{end_wait}
Please start cooking!{end_wait}
We came to build\nLord McCoy's palace.{page_break}No one's working\nthere now.{end_wait}
Something's wrong\nwith the old tree.{end_wait}
Do you think a tree\nspirit can curse a man?{end_now}
What's today's special?\nIt smells wonderful.{end_wait}
I asked Lord McCoy\nfor work.{page_break}Now I'm afraid\nto take the job.{end_wait}

Old songs say ancient
trees can grow strange
powers.{page_break}Maybe that power is what
caused{pause_20_skippable} the {text_effect:4}curse{reset_text_style}.{end_wait}
I don't believe\nin curses.{end_wait}
Travelers can't\ncontinue east.{page_break}At least the inn\nhas paying guests.{end_wait}
Mother, Father...\nPlease be safe.{end_wait}
Should I start cooking?\nI'm new here.{end_wait}
I've heard enough\ncomplaints for one day!{end_wait}
I'm starving.{page_break}And I still have\nto serve everyone else.{end_wait}
I came here to sell\nfurniture.{page_break}Now the palace work\nhas stopped.{end_wait}
So that's the tree\nthey call sacred.{end_wait}
I don't care how.\nJust end the curse.{end_wait}
Is the food ready?\nI'm hungry.{end_wait}
These stories\nare frightening me.{end_wait}
They say Tret lives\nin the sacred tree.{end_wait}
Lord McCoy is so shaken\nby the curse that he\ncan't eat.{end_wait}

The lord only sees brave,
mighty warriors.{page_break}You don't look the part.
Do you think you can do
the job?{end_now}
Lord McCoy is a hard\nman. Watch what you say\naround him.{end_wait}
The master's temper is\nshort. Don't keep him\nwaiting.{end_wait}
Nobody believed it could\nhappen. Then they all\nturned to wood.{end_wait}
Is there no one who can\nhelp us?{end_wait}
Lord McCoy won't hire\nsome scrawny kids.{end_wait}
To see Lord McCoy,\nfollow the red carpet.{end_wait}
Don't offend Lord McCoy.\nI'm warning you.{end_wait}
You'd really go into\nKolima Forest?{end_now}
I always said the old\ntree in Kolima Forest\nshould be left alone.{end_wait}
This is Lady McCoy's\nroom. Touch nothing.{end_wait}
How many times must I\ntell them? Why won't they\nleave me be?{end_wait}

Children shouldn't be
allowed in the palace!{page_break}If they break an urn,
I'm the one who gets
the blame!{end_wait}
Sending children into\nKolima Forest?{page_break}Do they want more\npeople cursed?{end_wait}

I should've kept quiet
when they planned the
new palace.{page_break}Maybe I'm the reason
they cut down the
holy tree...{end_wait}
The nerve! Walking into\nthe palace unescorted!{end_wait}

Milady was famous for her
beauty, far and wide.{page_break}That's why milord will
pay any price to please
her.{end_wait}
Someday I'll sleep in a\nsilk nightgown like this.{end_wait}
Will anyone ever make my\ndreams come true, like\nmilady's did?{end_wait}
Oh no. A hole in the\nnightgown. Milady will\nbe furious!{end_wait}

You can see Kolima from
here.{page_break}On sunny days, Lord
McCoy came to admire
the view.{end_wait}
The curse hasn't reached\nBilibin yet.\nNot yet.{end_wait}
Lord McCoy hasn't been\nhere in a long while.{page_break}It's the curse. What\nelse would keep him away?{end_wait}

Kolima Forest used to be
so green. After they cut
the holy tree,{page_break}everything turned brown.
Is the forest dying...?{end_wait}

Well? These are Bilibin's
great treasures.{page_break}Whoever ends the curse
may claim them as his
own.{end_wait}
We're giving our\ntreasure to these\nweaklings?{end_wait}
What use is treasure to\na man who's turned to\nwood?{end_wait}
Bah! Yeh're too young.\nYeh cannae handle this.{end_wait}
Are you serious,\n{actor_name:1}? That didn't\nbother you at all?{end_now}
Don't let him get to you.{page_break}We'll prove we can\nhandle this job, whatever\nit is.{end_wait}
Hey! No job done,\nno reward!{end_wait}
That's all I know.\nDon't ask again.{end_wait}
Shame. Come back when\nyou've grown a bit.{end_wait}

There's nothing more to
discuss!{page_break}Send them away. I don't
care how many times they
come back!{end_wait}
It's hard, being that\nyoung.{page_break}They dinnae ken what\nit means to be afraid.{end_wait}

That barricade's shoddy.
We built it in a rush.{page_break}The hinges are noisy
and weak. A good push
might break them.{end_wait}
I can't believe they let\nyou go. You're too young!{end_wait}
McCoy's Hidden Warehouse\nNo entry. Keep out!{end_wait}
Even frozen Imil must\nfeel warm with {actor_name:4}\nthere.{end_wait}
A tree... shaped like\na person. Disturbing.{end_wait}
They're... so heavy...\nI can't hold them much\nlonger.{end_wait}
No entry without a permit.\nBy order of Lord McCoy.{end_wait}
I was a tree for a\nwhile. Can you believe\nthat?{end_now}
Welcome to Bilibin.{pause_20_skippable}\nWe'll forget this curse\nbusiness soon enough.{end_wait}
The travelers from Imil?\nThey crossed the river.{end_wait}

The tree by the gate?
It's a man again.{page_break}Thank the gods. I
thought it'd stay that
way forever.{end_wait}

I saw Lord McCoy walking
the streets today,
first time in ages.{page_break}He must be relieved
the curse is broken.{end_wait}
The barricade on the\nKolima road is open\nagain, I hear.{end_wait}
Those three kids\ndisappeared in the middle\nof all that trouble.{end_wait}

Three young warriors
broke the curse.{page_break}Say... you wouldn't be
those warriors, would
you?{end_now}
McCoy's men say they saw\nthe ones who saved us.{end_wait}
Ever been to Imil, up\nnorth?{end_now}
The bottom is hidden\nfrom view. The well is\ndeeper than it looks.{end_wait}
